title: Lawn weed and fertiliser product boundaries
audience: Lawn and turf crew members, crew leaders and office staff who handle, quote or record weed control and fertiliser products on client lawns.
learningOutcomes: Describe the boundary between lawn maintenance, which the crew may do under the business's scope, and product application, which may need a licence or authority.
Read a product label and safety data sheet and identify the conditions of use that apply.
Store, handle and record weed and fertiliser products safely, including spill and drift control.
Refer any weed-control or fertiliser task that is outside the business's authority.

instruction.heading: Why product rules matter on a lawn
instruction.body: Weed control and fertiliser are among the most common requests from lawn clients, and they are also the easiest to get wrong. A product that is safe on the label can still harm people, pets, waterways, neighbouring gardens and the lawn itself if it is mixed wrongly, applied in wind, sprayed near a boundary or applied at the wrong rate. In many jurisdictions, applying some pesticides or herbicides to other people's property for payment is regulated, and the rules may depend on the type of product, the method and the setting. This lesson teaches you to recognise the boundary, read the product information and stop where the task is outside the business's authority. It does not grant any licence, certificate or authority to apply a regulated product.

instruction.heading: Where the boundary sits
instruction.body: Maintenance tasks such as mowing, edging, raking and watering are normal lawn work and are described in other lessons. Product application is different. Applying a weed killer, a selective herbicide, a broadleaf treatment, a fertiliser or a soil amendment is a separate task with its own risks. New South Wales has the clearest official position checked so far. The NSW Environment Protection Authority's fact sheet, dated August 2018, says that people who spray weeds commercially have needed a ground-applicator licence since 1 July 2018, and it places routine garden and lawn maintenance, including bindii spraying, within an amenity horticulture exemption. Check the rules where the job is located before any product is applied, and record the rule that applies. If the business is not authorised for product application in that location, offer the client the mowing and maintenance work only, and refer the product work to a licence holder who is authorised for it.

instruction.heading: Reading the label and the safety data sheet
instruction.body: Read the product label before opening the container. Look for the active ingredient, the target weeds, the approved crops or settings, the rate of use, the mixing instructions, the protective equipment, the re-entry period, the pets and people restrictions, the buffer distance from waterways and the storage and disposal instructions. Read the safety data sheet for the hazards, first-aid measures, fire-fighting, spill response and storage requirements. If the label and the safety data sheet do not agree, stop and refer. Do not use a product for a purpose the label does not cover. Keep the label and the safety data sheet with the product, and make them accessible to the crew at the job site. Record the product name, batch, rate and the area treated on the job record.

instruction.heading: Handling, storage and drift control
instruction.body: Store products in their original labelled containers, in a locked, ventilated and dry store, away from food, animals, children, heat and incompatible products. Never decant products into drink containers. Mix only the amount needed, and mix in a well-ventilated area, following the label. Apply products only in calm conditions, and check the forecast for wind. Keep spray drift away from neighbours, waterways, gardens and vehicles, and maintain the label's buffer distances. Keep people and pets off the treated area for the period stated on the label. Clean equipment after use, and dispose of rinse water and empty containers only as the label and the approved waste process allow. For any spill, stop, contain the spill with absorbent material, keep people back and inform the supervisor. Do not wash spilt product into a drain.

instruction.heading: Fertiliser and nutrient run-off
instruction.body: Fertilisers are usually applied to lawns to supply nutrients, and they can be a pollutant when they reach waterways. Apply fertiliser at the rate and in the manner that the product label specifies, and avoid application before heavy rain or onto hard surfaces, paths and drains. Sweep any spilt fertiliser back onto the lawn or into a suitable container, and do not wash it into the stormwater system. Keep fertiliser stored separately from weed products and in a dry place. Record the product, the rate and the area. Fertiliser recommendations should follow the client's soil and lawn assessment, not a standard schedule alone.

instruction.heading: Verification and escalation
instruction.body: A supervisor should check the product decision, the label, the record and the handling. A competent worker can name the product, state its conditions of use, identify whether the job is inside or outside the business's authority in that location, show the storage and the spill kit, and explain how they would manage drift. Escalate any request for a product that is outside the business's authority, any label that is unclear, any spill, and any product that is found without a label or safety data sheet.

procedure: Confirm whether the request is maintenance or product application, and check the rules for the job's state, territory and council.
If the job is product application and the business is not authorised for it at that location, offer the maintenance work only and refer the product work.
Read the label and the safety data sheet, and confirm the product, the target, the rate, the buffer and the re-entry period.
Check the wind forecast and the proximity of neighbours, pets, waterways and vehicles, and plan the application to avoid drift.
Wear the protective equipment specified on the label and the safety data sheet, and mix only the amount needed.
Apply the product in calm conditions, keep people and pets away, and maintain the buffer distance.
Store products in their labelled containers, locked and separate. Clean equipment and dispose of waste as the label allows.
Record the product, the batch, the rate, the area treated, the weather, the re-entry period and the client's acknowledgement.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks the crew to spray bindii across the whole front lawn and to fertilise the back lawn on the same visit. The forecast shows a moderate breeze and the neighbour's vegetable garden is on the fence line.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you check, and what do you offer the client?
workedExamples.reasoning: Check whether the business is authorised for product application at that location, under the rules for the state and council. Note that the breeze and the neighbour's garden are drift risks. If the business is authorised and the conditions are calm enough, plan the application with buffers and record it. If not, offer the mowing and maintenance work, refer the weed spraying to a licence holder, and reschedule the fertiliser for conditions with no heavy rain forecast.

workedExamples.situation: A worker finds an unlabelled container in the storage shed with a liquid that smells of solvent.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not open or use the container. Keep it separate, mark it, and inform the supervisor. Without a label or a safety data sheet the product cannot be used or disposed of safely. The supervisor decides the response, which may include contacting the supplier and following the business's hazardous-substances disposal route.

equipmentAndPpe: Product label and safety data sheet kept with the product
Protective equipment specified on the label, such as gloves, eye protection and coveralls
Calibrated application equipment, where the business is authorised to apply products
Locked, ventilated and dry storage for products
Spill kit with absorbent material and a labelled waste container

commonErrors.error: Applying a product because the client asked, without checking whether the business is authorised for that work at that location.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the rule for the job's location and offer maintenance only where product application is not authorised.

commonErrors.error: Spraying in a breeze close to a vegetable garden or waterway.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the wind, keep buffers, and stop when drift is possible.

commonErrors.error: Decanting a product into an unmarked bottle to save time.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep products in their labelled containers and mix only what is needed.

commonErrors.error: Washing a fertiliser spill into the stormwater drain.
commonErrors.prevention: Sweep spills back onto the lawn or into a container, and keep product away from drains.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Applying some weed-control and other pesticide products for payment may need a licence or authority. The NSW EPA's August 2018 fact sheet says people who spray weeds for payment need a ground-applicator licence, and treats routine garden and lawn maintenance as within an amenity horticulture exemption.
This lesson does not grant a pesticide or ground applicator licence, a certificate or any authority to apply regulated products.
Storage, handling and disposal of products fall under the model WHS framework's duties on hazardous chemicals.

qualityStandard: The job's product authority has been checked for the location, and the rule relied on is recorded.
Every product used has a label and safety data sheet at the site, and the label conditions are followed.
No product is applied in wind or near a neighbour, waterway or pet without a documented drift control.
Storage, spill control and disposal are recorded and meet the label instructions.
documentationEvidence: Authority check record for the job, including the jurisdiction and the rule relied on.
Product record with the name, batch, rate, area, weather, buffer and re-entry period.
Spill or incident record with the containment and the person informed.
Client acknowledgement of the product applied and the re-entry instructions.
summary: Mowing and maintenance are normal lawn work. Product application may need a licence or authority, and the rule depends on the location.
Read the label and safety data sheet before opening a product, and follow the conditions of use.
Control drift, keep buffers, and never wash product into a drain.
Refer product work that is outside the business's authority. This lesson does not grant any licence.

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks the crew to spray weeds on the lawn. What must be checked first?
options: Whether the business is authorised for product application at that location, under the rules that apply.
Whether the client has paid the deposit for the full season and the rest of the lawn work
Whether the neighbour's lawn needs the same product, since the two lawns share a fence line

knowledgeChecks.question: A product label gives a re-entry period and a buffer distance from waterways. What is correct?
options: Follow them where they are convenient for the job and the client's timetable this week and the weather
Follow them as written, keeping people and pets off the area for the re-entry period and maintaining the buffer.
Ignore them if the product is common and the job is small, since the risk is low anyway in most cases

knowledgeChecks.question: A fertiliser spill is on a driveway near a stormwater drain. What should the crew do?
options: Hose it into the drain to clear the driveway quickly before the client returns from work
Leave it for the rain to wash it away, since rain clears most spills off a driveway
Sweep it back onto the lawn or into a container and keep it away from the drain.
